newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt mkts rally into close as Kiwi strengthens.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt mkts rally into close as Kiwi strengthens.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD
OVERNIGHT CASH 7.95 PCT (PREV 8.00) US 5-YR 6.27 (PREV 6.29)
* NZ debt markets rally as TWI rises above 68.0
* Euro activity rumoured to be bolstering Kiwi, mid bonds
* Volume light, focus firmly on Friday's U.S. payrolls data
New Zealand debt markets rallied into Monday's close as the New Zealand dollar's Trade-Weighted Index rose above 68 late in the session.
"It's pretty positive right through the curve," said a money market dealer. "I think just the TWI above 68 has certainly sparked a bit of interest in the short end."
The 90-day bank bill rate rallied seven basis points to close at 7.84 percent. The TWI had eased a touch to 67.97 by the close.
The dealer said that if the TWI remained at around 68, there was no reason why the 90-days couldn't rally below 7.5 percent in the near term.
"If the TWI keeps its head up here, I think we'll rally into our CPI number," he said. Consumer Price Index inflation data is due on January 17.
In the bond market, yields were also six to seven basis points lower. Dealers said buying of short to mid bonds was rumoured to be on the back of euro activity.

"It's either the covering stuff that they didn't get to cover during the illiquid period over the last two or three weeks, or there's some fresh activity...maybe it's a combination of both," said one.
However, volumes had been light and the short term focus remained on U.S. payrolls data due on Friday.
